bug_semantics: The MISP-to-STIX page lets an operator connect cti-transmute to a remote MISP server. The server-side /misp_search_events proxy copied remote event id, info, date, organization, attribute count, threat level, tag name, and tag colour into JSON, after which the browser interpolated those values into tr.innerHTML, tag/TLP badge HTML, distribution-label HTML, and flash HTML. A malicious or compromised remote MISP instance could therefore return crafted markup or script-capable attributes that execute in the cti-transmute origin when the operator browses or imports events; unvalidated remote tag colours also reached CSS background values.
flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 introduced the remote-MISP browser end to end: the proxy that returned remote fields and the first HTML-interpolating renderers (showFlash, showTlpWarning, miTagBadges, and miRenderRows). Commit 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22 later expanded the same vulnerable rendering to multi-select IDs and sharing-group/distribution labels, but it did not originate the vulnerability because exploitable remote event fields already reached innerHTML in b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48.
ai_marker: absent on BIC b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48: git cat-file commit shows author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, one ordinary parent, the subject 'add: [misp connection] can connect to a misp instance and select event to import', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fh4x-m2h5-c6vx describes CWE-79 from remote MISP fields rendered by HTML interpolation, names affected/patched versions as Unknown, and links the closing commit https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/95e64137358d6fb7f1711523de2bf02ff6b181a7. In the validated clone, `git show b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/templates/convert/misp_to_stix.html` shows the newly added proxy returning `id`, `info`, `date`, `attribute_count`, `org`, `threat_level`, and remote tag `name`/`colour`, while the same commit adds `tr.innerHTML` with `${ev.info}`, `${ev.org}`, `${miTagBadges(ev.tags)}`, tag badges containing `${t.name}` and CSS `${bg}`, and showFlash interpolation. `git log --all -S'title="${ev.info||'` returns exactly b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 as addition and 95e64137358d6fb7f1711523de2bf02ff6b181a7 as removal; `git log -L 537,562:website/web/templates/conversions/misp_to_stix.html 666680b392e10e7bde61b43337755742b0fe1694` traces the row renderer to b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 and its later multi-select edits to 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22. Direct-parent check `git grep -n -e miRenderRows -e misp_search_events -e tagBadgesHtml -e '${ev.info' 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5 -- website/web/templates/convert/misp_to_stix.html website/web/convert/convert.py` has no matches; the BIC diff adds both routes and renderers, proving parent absence. `git show 95e64137358d6fb7f1711523de2bf02ff6b181a7` shows direct removal of all vulnerable row/badge/flash interpolation: new website/web/static/js/misp/mispEventRows.js uses createElement/textContent/setAttribute, validates colours with /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/, and misp_to_stix.html assigns remote flash/distribution text through textContent. Its parent 666680b392e10e7bde61b43337755742b0fe1694 still matches `${msg}`, `${tagHtml}`, and `title="${ev.info||`; those strings are absent at the fix. `git tag --contains b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` lists v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, whereas `git tag --contains 95e64137358d6fb7f1711523de2bf02ff6b181a7` lists only v1.5; merge-base checks confirm BIC absent from v1.2/present in v1.3 and fix absent from v1.4/present in v1.5. Thus repository tags establish vulnerable releases v1.3-v1.4 and first fixed release v1.5 even though the advisory does not declare package ranges. `git cat-file commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` provides the BIC-only AI check quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins with b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48, not with the later UI expansion or a rename: that atomic, single-parent feature commit first creates both the attacker-controlled remote data path and multiple executable HTML sinks, while its immediate parent has neither the MISP proxy nor the browser renderers. The 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22 additions increase the number of exposed fields but are descendants of an already exploitable flaw, so no squash decomposition is appropriate. The advisory-linked 95e64137358d6fb7f1711523de2bf02ff6b181a7 is a direct source fix against a still-vulnerable parent and closes the mechanism by replacing remote-derived markup with DOM text nodes and restricting colours; release ancestry puts that fix first in v1.5. Under the BIC-only rule, the human-named b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 commit object contains no canonical AI attribution or bot identity, so later commits and external metadata cannot make the root cause AI-attributed and the verdict is NOT_AI.
